I've been working this land since I was twenty years old. My father worked it before me. Four point one mu, same well, same rotation — wheat then maize, every year without fail. I don't need to think too hard about this. My hands know what to do.

**My reasoning as this farmer:**

The land is all in rotation — the same 4.1 mu does wheat in winter, then maize in summer. That's how we've always done it here in Quzhou. You finish the wheat in June, you get the maize in before the rains come. By October, you're harvesting maize and turning the ground over for wheat again. The cycle doesn't change.

For **wheat**, I'll buy improved seed from the township seed shop — the same Jimai variety I've used the past several years. It's reliable. I'll rotary till after maize harvest in October, get the base fertilizer down — some diammonium phosphate and urea mixed in — then plant. Come spring at jointing, I'll top-dress with more urea. I'll run the well pump three times: once before winter sets in to help the roots, once at jointing in April, once more around heading in May when it's dry. Two rounds of spraying — one herbicide early on, one for aphids and rust later. Should get around 430 jin per mu. That's normal for us here.

For **maize**, I'll buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever's similar at the shop this year, same as always. After wheat harvest I'll rotary till quickly and get it in the ground. Summer rains help, but I'll pump water twice if it gets dry — once when the seedlings are establishing, once at grain filling if needed. I apply more fertilizer on maize than wheat — split into base and side-dress at big bell stage. Two pesticide passes, one for weeds, one for borer. Expect around 520 jin per mu.

Two of us eating, selling the surplus. This is how I've kept the family fed for fifty years.
